dialogueNodes.nodeText: I can't say I've seen you around here before, stranger. What brings you to the once-great city of Crestmourn?

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: I'm looking for work. Know of anything?
I've heard things are bad here. I've come to help.
Oh, I'm just sightseeing.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: You've come at a particularly bad time, I'm afraid. The whole city's been taken over by those wretched Followers of Bolothamogg.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: The Followers of who, now?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: That's a nice sentiment, but take it from me -- you don't want to mess with the Followers of Bolothamogg.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: The Followers of who, now?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: We shouldn't really be talking about this... They don't like it when you say the name. Listen, if it's a gig you want, maybe we can work something out.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: I'm listening.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: You see that gentleman in the corner? That's Quinton, he usually sorts out the entertainment here. Worth a shot speaking to him, I should think. Tell him Samaren sent you over.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Thanks, Samaren. I will.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: ... Do I know you?

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Not yet, but you -- and everyone in this tavern -- soon will.
I'm passing through, looking for work. Samaren sent me over, told me you might help me get a gig here.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Excellent, another bard with an inflated ego. Just what this city needs.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: It sounds like the city needs a lot of things. Who are these Followers I heard about?
So... do I have the job?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: I think we can arrange something. The Followers make it hard for us these days, but we make it work.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Who are they? These Followers?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Devotees and fanatics of the ancient 'protector' of our fair city, the god Bolothamogg.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: And what do they want?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: They want what we all want: for fortune to return to Crestmourn. But they believe the only way to do this is by appeasing their god.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: And appeasing gods never involves baking cupcakes, it seems.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Hah, I like you. No, it doesn't. They want to strip away everything that makes our city beautiful, our art, our music, our entire culture.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Hence why it's hard to get a gig around here.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Exactly. Anyway, why don't you come with me and we'll get you settled.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Sounds like a plan.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Something doesn't feel right...

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: What's going on?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: They're already here! I hope you can do more than sing, kid.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Oh, for --

dialogueNodes.nodeText: You know, I just met you and all. But I was really expecting you to have my back in there.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: What do you mean?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: You left me hanging, kid. I asked for help, and you didn't help.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: I'm sorry, Quinton... It won't happen again.
Rhesa helps those who help themselves.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Yea, alright. I'll let it slide this once. Folks like us, we need to stick together, you know.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: I agree. How about I buy you a drink, let me make up for it?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Oh, don't give me that. You know what? You can forget the gig. Get out of here, haunt someone else's bar.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Fine. The place reeks anyway.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Now you're talking. Let's go, kid, I hear Samaren's pouring Dwarvish Fire tonight.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Now that sounds like a good time.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: You know, I just met you and all. So I appreciate you having my back in there.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Think nothing of it, Quinton. We artists have to stick together.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: We don't get many people like you these days. Anyway. How about I buy you a drink, in thanks?

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: That sounds like a plan to me.
I usually stay away from mind-altering drugs.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: I heard Samaren's pouring Dwarvish Fire tonight. All sorts of raucous revelry will surely ensue.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Well, what are we waiting for?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Oh, Rhesa... Well, to each their own. I'll drink, and you can watch. Maybe we can swap stories.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Yeah, I can get behind that. Lead the way, Quinton!

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Ignore any skeletons you see poking out of the crop be- oh you need something?

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Buy
Leave

dialogueNodes.nodeText: To herb or not to herb? That is the question.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Buy
Leave

dialogueNodes.nodeText: You want plants? I have plants. I also have things made with plants if you’re so inclined.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Buy
Leave

dialogueNodes.nodeText: You know, I just met you and all. So I appreciate you having my back in there.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Think nothing of it, Quinton. We artists have to stick together.
Have the Followers done something like this before?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: That was… unexpected. And worrisome. I think we best go tell Samaren what happened here, see if she knows anything about this.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Yeah, of course, Quinton. Let’s go.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Not like this, no. They’re usually more subtle. I think we best go tell Samaren what happened here, see if she knows anything about this.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Yeah, of course, Quinton. Let’s go.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Are you alright, darlin'? You look a little worse for wear. I heard some bangin' and crashin' from the backroom...

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: There were a couple of Followers in your back room… They jumped us when we were getting ready for our gig.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Gods protect us! I dunno how those ruffians got in here, but you and Quinton both have my sincerest thanks for dealin' with them.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Do you have any idea what they were doing here?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: I haven't a clue, I'm afraid… But whatever their interest, can't be good for business. I'm up to my ears in work 'round here, but if you can figure out what their plans are, I'll be in your debt.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: I think we can manage that. Any idea on where to start sniffing around?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: As a matter of fact, I do. Whenever strangers come to town, you can bet yer last gold coin the Guild of Shadows knows somewhat about them.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: The Guild of Shadows?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Yea, you know… Less than upstandin' brokers of rumors and jobs, if yer catchin' my drift…

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Criminals, you mean?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Naw, not strictly speaking, they just have a… healthy skepticism about the law. Problem is, they're very reclusive. You'll hafta do some heavy digging to find them. Couldn't hurt to ask some of the folk 'round town. Or, force them to find you. You make a big enough name for yourself, I'm sure they'll take an interest in you, too.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Well, it’s a start. Better get going.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Good luck, darlin'. And be careful. The Guild of Shadows ain't nothin' to trifle with. C'mon back if you need a drink or a place to rest.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: I'll keep that in mind. Thanks, Samaren.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Well now, what can I do for you? You look like you've got something on your mind.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: You wouldn't happen to know anything about the Guild of Shadows, would you?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: How about we keep our voices low, eh? The Guild of Shadows... you're asking about some mighty shady folk there, friend. Best not to get tangled up in their affairs. They deal in things best left untouched.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: But I need to know more. The Followers have been causing trouble here, and who can say what they'll be emboldened to do next?
I'm not afraid of a little danger. I need to know where they meet.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Now, now, I don't get involved in such things. But if you're really determined to learn more… there's a kobold in town named Mudd. He's got a nose for trouble, and might know a thing or two about the Guild. Though, you'll have to pry the information out of him. He's not exactly the most trusting sort.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Mudd? I'll try my luck. Thanks.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Just remember my warning. The Guild of Shadows isn't something to be taken lightly.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: I'll be cautious. Thanks again.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Sure, sure... You won't be saying that when you're staring down the wrong end of a dagger. Take my advice, stranger, and leave it.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Yea... I'll keep that in mind.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Greetings, esteemed adventurer. I trust your journey has been most… invigorating? No, no, 'invigorating' is far too pedestrian. Perhaps 'galvanizing'? Or, dare I say, 'electrifying'?

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: I'm looking for information on the Guild of Shadows.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Ah, the Guild of Shadows. A most enigmatic organization. Their methods are perplexing, their motives convoluted. One could almost say they are… shrouded in mystery! Though, 'cloaked' might be more appropriate.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: I need to know more. I suspect they're involved in some trouble.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Trouble? My, what a mundane word. 'Turmoil', perhaps? Or 'chaos'? The Guild of Shadows certainly stirs the pot of… unpredictability. Though, 'brewing' might be a more suitable metaphor.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: I'm not interested in your wordplay. I need information, and I suspect you have some.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Information? Such a limited term. 'Knowledge', perhaps? Or 'insight'? I, Mudd, am a veritable repository of… hmm… knowledge! Though, 'fountain' might be more evocative.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Enough with the riddles! I need to know where the Guild of Shadows meets.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Ah, their rendezvous. A most secretive affair. Their locations are ever-shifting, their presence ephemeral. One could almost say they are… ghosts! No, 'phantoms' is more accurate.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Just tell me where they meet! I'm running out of patience.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Very well, very well. Patience, my dear adventurer, is a virtue. Though, 'endurance' might be more fitting. Let me ponder… Ah, yes! They have been known to congregate in a most peculiar location. A dilapidated structure by the docks. One could almost say it is… haunted! Though, 'infested' might be more accurate.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: A dilapidated structure by the docks? I'll check it out. Thanks, Mudd.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: You are welcome. Or perhaps 'delighted' is more appropriate. Now, if you'll excuse me, I must contemplate the profound nature of existence. Or perhaps simply 'ponder'...

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: I'll leave you to your… contemplations. Farewell, Mudd.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Greetings, my good sir! I am Alera, a thespian of the highest caliber, and I require your assistance with a most pressing matter.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: A thespian? What kind of assistance do you require?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Ah, mere formalities! I am in the midst of producing a play, a grand tragedy, a masterpiece of dramatic tension! But alas, it lacks a certain… something.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: What kind of play is it?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: It is a tale of woe, of betrayal, of revenge! A young man, wronged by his uncle, seeks justice! But I call it... "Whamlet!"

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: Whamlet? What a strange name.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Indeed! But to truly capture the essence of this tragic tale, I require a prop, a symbol of mortality, a touch of the macabre...

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: What kind of prop?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: A skull, my good sir! A skull! Imagine, if you will, the young Whamlet, holding aloft the skull of his dear departed court jester, lamenting the cruel twists of fate!

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: A skull? Where would I even find one?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Ah, that's where your assistance comes in! I require the expertise of someone with a discerning eye and a… certain… resourcefulness.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: I see. What kind of resourcefulness are we talking about?

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Let us just say that theatrical productions sometimes require... unconventional methods of acquiring props. You understand? Discretion is paramount, of course.

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: I understand. I'll do my best to find a suitable skull. Though I can't promise anything.

dialogueNodes.nodeText: Excellent! This is just what I needed! You have been a tremendous help, my good sir. I shall be sure to send you an invitation to the premiere!

nodeResponses.nodeResponseText: I'll look forward to it. Break a leg!
